# Micro-test design: api-error-messages sentence change

Status: DESIGN ONLY. Nothing has been run.

## Question

Does "Say what went wrong and the next step the caller can take." make agents write error messages that
include a next step, where "Say what went wrong." did not (baseline: 6 of 10 runs had none)?

Failure type: the agent complies but omits an element. The change is a wording swap inside the existing
instruction, so the test is a head-to-head of the two sentences with everything else identical.

## Arms

| Arm | Context |
|---|---|
| OLD | Full current `skills/api-error-messages/SKILL.md`, unchanged. |
| NEW | The same file with only the one sentence replaced. Check with `diff`: exactly one line differs. |

OLD is the control. The earlier baseline is not reused as the control unless its model, flags, prompt and
isolation are shown to match this design. Otherwise re-run OLD in the same batch, so both arms share the
same setup and the same day.

## Models (chosen by me; say if you want others)

- `claude-sonnet-5-5`
- `claude-haiku-5-5`

Same number of reps on each: 10 reps per arm per model, 40 reps in all. A wording that binds one model
can fail on the other, so the verdict is per model.

## Task prompt

Reuse the baseline's task prompt word for word, so the OLD arm can be compared with the baseline. If it
is not on hand, use: "Write the JSON error response for a 404 returned by POST /orders when `customer_id`
'c_91' does not exist. Reply with the JSON only." The prompt must not mention next steps, fixes or
guidance.

## Isolation (Claude Code only, no API key)

Each rep is a separate `claude -p` call, one sample per call.

- Run from a new empty directory outside every repository.
- No tools. Turn off user settings, CLAUDE.md files and memory.
- Put the skill text in the system prompt, and the task as the user message.
- I have not checked the exact flags. The reference points to the newest `specs/baseline/*/kit/`, and
  that directory does not exist in this repo. Before the first rep, check the flags against
  `claude --help` and write them into the runner.
- Pilot first: one throwaway rep that asks what context it can see (instruction files, memory, tools,
  other sessions, the user's name). If anything is unplanned, fix the setup and repeat the pilot. Pilot
  output is never scored.
- Keep this spec, the proposal and the baseline records out of each rep's reach.

## Rules (registered before any reply is read; commit this file first)

Per rep, grade the `message` text.

- **PASS:** the message names a specific next step the caller can take: a value to send, an endpoint to
  call, or a named action, such as "create the customer with POST /customers first".
- **FAIL:** the message gives only the cause, or its only next step is vague ("check your request",
  "see the docs", "try again").
- **VOID:** the rep read a file or used a tool, the reply has no message, or the isolation leaked. A void
  rep is replaced by a fresh rep. The void count is reported.

Secondary checks, reported and not part of the verdict:

- The message is under 200 characters. The new sentence could push messages over the limit.
- Field, value and rule appear in that order, where they apply.
- The message names no internal class or stack frame.

Success: in each model, NEW passes at least 9 of 10, and passes at least 4 more reps than OLD. If NEW
passes on one model and not on the other, the wording is not adopted as it stands. If a reply shows a
reading these rules did not foresee, keep the registered verdict and report the counts under both
readings.

## Blind scoring

- The runner writes each reply to a sheet with a random ID. Nothing on the sheet (name, path, order,
  length of the file name, count) shows arm or model.
- The mapping from ID to arm and model goes in a separate file that the grader does not open.
- A fresh Claude Code session grades the sheets against the rules above. It has not seen the proposal.
- I read every FAIL and every borderline PASS myself. I unblind only after every sheet has a grade.

## Spend

No API key means these runs use Claude Code's own billing. I cannot see its per-call cost in advance.

- Cap: $1.00 of the $1.50 remaining. The rest is a reserve for replacing void reps and re-grading.
- Run the pilot, then one batch of 4 reps (one per arm per model), and record the cost of each batch.
- Stop rule: stop when the running total plus the worst-case cost of the next batch would pass the cap.
  Use the most expensive batch so far as the worst case.
- If the full 40 reps do not fit, cut the reps equally across all four cells and report the smaller
  count. Do not drop a model.

## Output

A table of PASS, FAIL and VOID counts per arm per model, the secondary checks, the cost per batch, and
the verdict under the registered rules.
